title: Reject specified first corrections with actual-law shell events
statement: For g_i(x)=sin(x_i) and fixed positive tau,eta, the exact independent-time first covariance correction has TV error tending to1 whenever deterministic positive integer allocations satisfy n+4k=o(d^(1/3)). With independent uniform times on disjoint strata, the corresponding obstruction is n+4k=o(d^(1/4)); its general upper bound remains d^(1/3), leaving a gap.

requires: Exactly the specified first correction and deterministic n(d),k(d)
Fixed positive noise scales and the smooth conservative sine family
provides: Actual-law separating shell events, surrogate-error control and all deterministic allocation subsequences
assumptions: Excludes the second correction, arbitrary adaptive/random allocations and other samplers
Analytic mean/g(0) solves this supplied family exactly
No sharp epsilon dependence or stratified d^(1/4) sufficiency
costs: Per-action surrogate squared error O(log(2d)); caps are asymptotic premises
Saved shell frequencies are diagnostics, not the general proof
contract.units: Full TV tending to1 and architecture-local query exponents
contract.obstruction: Not an information-theoretic N687 lower bound or family hardness result.

evidence.quote: not a lower bound for N687
evidence.range_scope: Actual-law shell separation for specified deterministic first-correction allocations.

evidence.quote: a variance comparison, not a factor-of-48 TV or runtime improvement
evidence.range_scope: Stratification preserves law/cap; separate variance and architecture obstruction.

body: Covariance alone cannot prove TV separation. Conditional concentration, nondegenerate common-time fluctuations and shrinking target shells supply the extra obligation.

review.scope: Actual completed audit is a separate version-bound overlay.
